svg.text: 1. Corrupted data
indecipherable bytes, rare; faulty serialisers (Fig 18-1)
2. No schema
no types, names or limits, so good and bad are
indistinguishable (Fig 18-2)
3. Invalid schema
SchemaId matches no registry schema: deleted, or an ID
from a staging registry (Fig 18-3)
4. Incompatible evolution
deserialises but cannot convert to the consumer's
schema after a breaking change (Fig 18-4)
5. Logically invalid value
an array for first_name, null in a non-nullable field
(Fig 18-5); implicit conventions, homemade libraries
6. Valid but semantically wrong
a negative cost, 'Robert'); DROP TABLE Students; --' as a
name (Fig 18-6); log and file parsers, messy phone numbers
7. Missing events
nothing produced when something should have been;
easy to prevent by testing; hurts event sourcing
8. Events that should not exist
duplicates after a producer restart: a delta counted twice, an
inflated analytics count, a double order (Fig 18-7)
Idempotent production (the Kafka idempotent producer) stops duplicates from retries but cannot fence out duplicates that are logically indistinguishable from other
events. Three strategies, in order: prevention (schemas, testing, validation, fail fast and gracefully), event design (corrections overwriting bad data), and rewind,
rebuild and retry as a last resort.
